$comment: Single source of truth for the Unity version this fork tests against, read by tools/check-unity-versions.* and (when enabled) .github/workflows/unity-tests.yml. Upstream CoplayDev runs a four-version GameCI matrix; this fork does not. Unity CI is disabled_manually here and all testing is local, so the matrix was reduced to the one version TestProjects/UnityMCPTests is actually saved by. That project is a Unity 6.5 project now: once saved by 6000.5.5f1 an older editor can no longer open it, so adding older rows back would only produce failures. Restoring a real matrix means first reverting TestProjects/UnityMCPTests/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt to the floor.
$dockerNote: --docker mode is unavailable at this version: GameCI publishes no unityci/editor:ubuntu-6000.5.x-* image (https://hub.docker.com/r/unityci/editor). tools/check-unity-versions.sh --docker will fail at the image pull, and unity-tests.yml could not run 6000.5 even if it were re-enabled. A local Unity Hub install is the only supported runner.
$coverageGap: Inverted relative to upstream. The UNITY_6000_5_OR_NEWER branches (UnityObjectIdCompat.cs EntityId path, UnityFindObjectsCompat.cs, UnityTypeConverters.cs) are now exercised — they previously compiled nowhere. What is no longer exercised: the legacy branches taken when UNITY_2022_*/UNITY_6000_0..4_OR_NEWER are off or only partially on, and the 2021.3 floor that MCPForUnity/package.json still declares in its 'unity' field. Those stay covered upstream, not here.
$defaultVersionComment: Must match TestProjects/UnityMCPTests/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt. local_harness.py reads that file first and only falls back to this value when it is missing.

versions.notes: Unity 6.5 — the version TestProjects/UnityMCPTests is saved by and the only one that can open it. UNITY_2022_*/UNITY_2023_*/UNITY_6000_0..5_OR_NEWER ON; UNITY_6000_6_OR_NEWER OFF. Note 6.5 escalates Object.GetInstanceID() from CS0618 (warning) to CS0619 (error) — route calls through UnityObjectIdCompat.GetInstanceIDCompat().
